text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: CRITICAL — High 5xx rate in region az2 for model-x (PD#PD12345). Root: spike in 502/504s on inference nodes. Link: https://pagerduty.example/pd/PD12345

pagerduty-bot: Auto-assign -> sre-oncall (acknowledged) :white_check_mark:

sre-oncall: Acked. seeing ~18% 5xx on /v1/generate for model-x in az2, other regions look nominal.

emma: Pulling logs now — running a short query.

raj: status on autoscaler? last logs showed a surge of scale events but pods kept terminating. could be OOM or eviction.

eng-runtime-lead: Noting concurrent KV cache evictions in az2, repeated OOMs in the VM logs around 12:02 UTC. Might be memory leak or sudden seq-length pressure.

sre-oncall: here's tail from one failing pod: ```
[2026-02-15T12:01:58Z] infer: allocation failed: out of memory
[2026-02-15T12:02:01Z] kubelet: eviction signal: memory.available
[2026-02-15T12:02:03Z] infer: attempt restart (crashloop)
```

emma: Confirmed, three pods in az2 in CrashLoopBackOff. Node pressure looks high. Checking node-level metrics.

ops-lead: Are dedicated customer pools affected or only hosted? Need to know customer impact ASAP.

customer-success: Early check: 8 hosted customers reporting 5xxs via support tickets, two enterprise customers reported latency spikes but no data loss. We'll draft an incident banner if we need to escalate customer comms.

sre-oncall: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Remove az2 from routing weights (failover) 2) Prewarm az3 fallback capacity if not already prewarmed 3) Temp rate-limit heavy concurrent clients to protect runtime 4) Investigate root cause of OOM/crashloop. Anyone object?

eng-runtime-lead: Agreed. I'll trigger a targeted routing rule to move traffic off az2 to az3/az1. Executing now: ```curl -X POST -d '{"region":"az2","weight":0}' https://routing.internal/api/v1/weights```

pagerduty-bot: Incident note added: routing change initiated by eng-runtime-lead at 12:08 UTC.

sre-oncall: Routing change in flight — watching for errors.

emma: Prewarm job kicked off for az3: ```/bin/prewarm --model model-x --gpu 4 --timeout 300``` — started at 12:09 UTC.

raj: Autoscaler logs show repeated scale-up then node termination sequences. I suspect a GPU driver fault causing node reboots. Node-level kernel Oops in syslog. Tagging infra team.

eng-runtime-lead: Ops, please open a cloud provider ticket for possible instance-level eviction/driver crash. I can roll back to a previous runtime build in az2 if needed, but prefer failover while we investigate.

ops-lead: Cloud ticket opened: CT-78921. Provider confirms they're investigating noisy host events in az2. ETA unknown.

sre-oncall: Current customer impact: ~12% global error-rate increase for hosted API, az2 specifically 85% of errors. No data loss for dedicated pools. Customer comms: draft incident banner to hosted API customers. customer-success pls prepare PSAT.

customer-success: Drafting banner now. Short note: "We're experiencing degraded inference availability in one region. We're routing traffic away and working on mitigation. No action required from customers." Will share for approval.

emma: Monitoring shows error-rate dropping in az2 after routing change (now 502s reduced ~70%), overall API error-rate creeping down. Continuing to monitor for regression.

sre-oncall: Alright — next steps: 1) Keep az2 out of rotation until root cause found or nodes recovered 2) Work with infra to replace affected hosts / file a kernel/driver rollback if needed 3) Follow up with PagerDuty incident updates every 15m and log all actions

eng-runtime-lead: I'll capture heap/dump artifacts from crashlooped pods for the runtime team and start a canary rollback plan for az2 if we see node stability issues persist after infra actions.

raj: Handoff plan: I'm on until 12:40 UTC, then hand to raj (2nd shift) — actually I'm raj, sorry: handing to emma at 12:40 UTC. emma, you're up for next 2 hours?

emma: I can take the handoff. Leaving a templatized note: "az2: removed from rotation, CT-78921 opened with provider, prewarm in az3, routing weight=0 applied, PD#PD12345 open"

sre-oncall: Thanks. tagging for followup: @eng-runtime-lead to post a short root-cause update in this thread when available; @ops-lead for cloud provider resolution notes.

pagerduty-bot: PD#PD12345 status: acknowledged -> under-investigation; next escalation timer stopped.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Action items summary (sre-oncall): [1] Keep az2 out of routing until stability confirmed. [2] Collect crash dumps + infra logs. [3] Monitor customer impact & update comms. [4] Schedule postmortem after recovery.

eng-runtime-lead: Noted. I'll post back within 30m with initial findings.

customer-success: Banner posted at 12:18 UTC. Will update if we open a wider incident page.

sre-oncall: Closing temporary PD path for now — we'll keep internal thread open until resolved. If anyone sees a regression, ping PD again.

emma: update: az2 error-rate ~down to baseline for some routes but a couple of legacy endpoints still showing sporadic 5xx. continuing checks.

sre-oncall: Thanks team. Handoff to emma at 12:40 UTC recorded.

emma: taking over — will post next status at 12:30 and at 12:50 or sooner if anything changes.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from eng-runtime-lead, :eyes: from ops-lead)
